I. Reuerendo in Christo patri et domino . . . abbati Cysterciensi totique conuentui ordinis eiusdem W. de Rosenberch marscalcus Boemie sinceram et paratam ad obsequia uoluntatem. Habentes in desiderio pro nostra nostrorumque progenitorum et successorum salute et remedio animarum abbatiam uestri ordinis conslruere et fundare, discretioni uestre significamus, quod inuocata sancti spi- ritus gratia presente venerabili abbute et quibusdam fratribus de Ylaria de consensu et expressa uoluntate coniugis nostre et aliorum amicorum nostrorum ad hoc locum distinximus satis aptum, uolentes eum predicto abhati de Ylaria et eins ecclesie tanquam matri filiam in perpetuum obedire. Dotauimus etiam locum supradictum reddi- tibus sexaginta talenta plene persoluentibus, addentes duas uineas cum piscationibus pascuis et nemoribus spatiosis, in proposito tenen- tes de die in diem nosfra possibilitate eosdem redditus augmentare. Quare douotionem uestram petimus studiose, quatenus antedictum locum uestro ordini incorporare dignemini propter deum. 1. entries.english:
The abbot and convent of the Cistercians at Cîteaux are asked by W. von Rosenberg to incorporate his new foundation at Hohenfurt into their order.

I, W. de Rosenberch, marshal of Bohemia, offer sincere and ready service to the reverend father in Christ and lord, the abbot of Cîteaux, and to the whole convent of that order. Desiring, for the salvation and remedy of the souls of ourselves, our ancestors, and our successors, to build and found an abbey of your order, we inform your discretion that, invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit and in the presence of the venerable abbot and certain brothers of Wilhering, with the consent and express will of my wife and our other friends, we have selected a sufficiently suitable place for this purpose. We wish it forever to obey the aforesaid abbot of Wilhering and his church as a daughter does her mother. We have also endowed the aforesaid place with revenues yielding sixty talents in full, adding two vineyards with fisheries, pastures, and extensive woods, and we intend to increase those revenues from day to day according to our means. Therefore, we earnestly ask your devotion to deign, for God’s sake, to incorporate the aforesaid place into your order.

According to Stülz, History of Wilhering, p. 530, no. 52: “The crumbled seal,” he remarks, “depicts the torso of an armed man with a sword in his right hand.” Compare the description of the seal on charter no. VIII. References: Stülz, same work; Millauer, p. 5; Proschko, p. 1.
